summary: Clicks outlive their link because the database never enforces the ON DELETE CASCADE declared in the schema
root_cause: SQLite enforces foreign keys per connection and only when 'PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON' is issued. LinkRepository never issues it, so deleting a link leaves its click rows behind. Analytics are looked up by code alone, so a re-created alias inherits them.

impacted.reason: Connection setup: enable foreign key enforcement and run the one-time orphan clean-up migration
Relies solely on the cascade; must delete the link's clicks explicitly
Where the symptom appears (aggregates by code). Reviewed, no change needed
Calls repo.delete. Reviewed, no change needed
Alias reuse path re-adds the same code. Reviewed, no change needed

data_flows: DELETE -> ShortenerService.delete -> LinkRepository.delete -> links row removed, clicks rows left behind (bug)
POST alias -> LinkRepository.add -> stats(code) counts the old clicks (symptom)
data_migration: Existing databases may hold orphaned clicks: purge them at startup with a single idempotent statement
risks: The purge deletes data: only rows with no parent link, which no API can reach
Startup time grows with the size of the clicks table (one anti-join on an indexed column)
out_of_scope: Authentication or ownership checks on delete
